paragraphs: Brighton & Hove City Council runs its own fostering service for the city, and the services that list Brighton and Hove as an area they cover are shown above. The council says it tries to place children with its own carers first so they can stay near their family, friends and school, and that many of its carers transferred to it from independent agencies.

The council's fostering booklet, updated in December 2025, says children who need foster care range from newborn babies to 18-year-olds, and many come as part of a group of brothers and sisters. It says the city is short of carers who share the cultural or ethnic background of the children coming into care, and asks more Black, Asian and racially minoritised people to come forward. Alongside short-term, long-term, parent and child and respite fostering, it offers Fostering Plus for young people moving from residential care into a family, and specialist care for young people seeking asylum. It started the Mockingbird model of linked fostering households in March 2025.

The council says becoming an approved carer takes about six months: an information event, a home visit, checks including an enhanced DBS check and a medical, the Skills to Foster course, a Form F assessment and a fostering panel. New carers are matched with an experienced buddy carer and a supervising social worker, and there is an out-of-hours service every day of the year. Pay is a weekly professional fee plus an allowance for the child that depends on their age and the type of fostering; the council's payments calculator gives the current figures. Carers already approved elsewhere can transfer, which it says typically takes four to five months.
The East Sussex and West Sussex pages list more services nearby.
